topics.label: Welcome and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: These framing remarks introduce the course structure, student audience, and core learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Biological Nature of Cancer and Research Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a disease of accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal differentiation and tissue architecture, along with the methods used to study tumor cells in vitro.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Benign versus Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts of tumor invasion and metastasis, illustrating how benign and malignant lesions differ histologically, functionally, and throughout stepwise disease progression.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue types.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological and anatomical mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer Epidemiology and Comparative Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and prevalence of various cancer types across human populations and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale, histological targets, and practical challenges of population screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Conclusion and Lecture Wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding remarks review the learning outcomes and provide administrative details for upcoming practicals and lectures.
